tip: Gwell (better) is the irregular comparative of da (good). You never say da-ach. Pair it with na (than).
A direct object soft-mutates after a short-form verb: brecwast becomes frecwast in Bwytais i frecwast.
Os (if) for a real condition takes the future. Daw means he'll come, the irregular future of dod (to come).
llai means less or fewer and is irregular, not built with -ach. Here siwgr llai is less sugar.
A feminine noun soft-mutates after the article y or yr: gorsaf (station) becomes yr orsaf.
Short adjectives add -ach for the comparative: tal (tall) becomes talach, shown here as dalach after yn.
Er mwyn plus a verb-noun means in order to: Er mwyn cael is in order to get.
iau (younger) is the irregular comparative of ifanc (young), not ifancach. Than is na.
Than is nag before a vowel and na before a consonant. Awr starts with a vowel, so llai nag awr.
po plus a superlative builds the more or the -er: Gorau po gyntaf means the sooner, the better.
Longer adjectives take mwyaf (most) in front for the superlative: mwyaf poblogaidd is most popular.
Front the subject and follow it with sy'n to say it is X who: Fy mam sy'n means it's my mum who.
Longer adjectives use yn fwy plus adjective plus na for more...than: yn fwy parod na fi, more willing than me.
Ar ôl i plus a subject plus a verb-noun means after X did; the verb soft-mutates, so pasio becomes basio.
Most superlatives end in -af: pwysig (important) becomes pwysicaf, the most important.
Dylai means should or ought to, so Dylai fe is he should. Its verb-noun soft-mutates: cael becomes gael.
Need uses angen plus ar, so the need sits on the person. Arnon ni means on us, so we needed it.
Pe is if for an unreal condition: Pe bawn i means if I were, and byddwn i is I would.
The word na (than) triggers aspirate mutation, so Caerdydd becomes na Chaerdydd.
hŷn (older) is the irregular comparative of hen (old), not henach. Than is na.
Use yn llai plus an adjective for less...: yn llai llawn means less full.
The word o (of) triggers soft mutation: cyllid (funding) becomes mwy o gyllid, more funding.
